description.narrative: Our Voices Our Futures (OVOF) partners bring extensive experience of lobbying and advocacy at multiple levels to a range of issues connected to gender, sexuality and digital rights. OVOF partners ensure that ground-level evidence and lived realities of structurally silenced women feed directly into lobbying and advocacyat every level and international-level advocacy is translated back into community-level work in the six countries. More international and national-level law and policymakers need to acknowledge and address the issue of growing authoritarianism (and its impact on civic space, democracy and the lives of structurally silenced women) and the increasing influence of anti-gender and anti-rights actors within international and national policy and legal spaces. Key Dutch actors will be mobilised to collaborate with and support Women Human Rights Defenders, LBT activists and sex workers’ rights movements by creating and opening spaces for their participation in international processes such as the Commission on the Status of Women and the Human Rights Council so that their voices will be heard.

FFP Panel titled “Transformative Approaches to Feminist Resourcing” : UHAI represented the OVOF Consortium in the panel discussion organised by the Count Me In! Consortium. Our contribution was focused on underpinning the need for more and better resourcing that sustains movements led by structurally silenced communities/women. UHAI specified the components of this resourcing as being: long term, flexible and sustained core support. We described our feminist value of approaching listening from a political perspective - listening is also a political act. Our contribution urged funders and allied partners to SSW/C movements to be deliberate about considering their political privilege and power when engaging with different voices and communities in the SSW/C movements - always asking “ who are the marginalised within the marginalised?” since SSW/C movements are not homogenous. We shared that funding should not perpetuate the already existing power dynamics. The nature of crisis in our region points to evidence showing that crisis does not happen in a vacuum - it is primarily orchestrated and sustained by political, economic and social structures. Our submission concluded by highlighting that while responding to safety and security needs of SSW/C communities is important, of even greater importance is SSW/C movement building and sustenance of movement infrastructure.
The CFCS Conference is held every 2 years and was not meant to take place in 2022.

The 8th Changing Faces, Changing Spaces Conference will be held in May 2023. The CFCS is curated by an activist task-force which includes Structurally Silenced Women and brings together activists and funders resourcing LGBTIQ+ and Sex Workers' movements across the Continent to take stock and strategise together on activism and resourcing the Continent. This result will be captured in the 2023 annual reporting. OVOF partners organised a session on technology and movement building for Structurally Silenced Persons in Africa.

1 meeting in Kenya at Dutch Embassy.

Engagement with the Dutch Embassy through key spaces such as the Partner Days hosted by the Dutch ambassadors in Kenya. The key conversations focused on strengthening the intersectional approach on resourcing structurally silenced communities to build their capacity to advocate for and raise awareness on the rights of SSW/SSC (structurally silenced women / communities). Due to the current hostile and dynamic operating environment in Uganda, our partners were not able to effectively engage the Dutch embassy on advocacy priorities-the impact of the AHA2023 on our communities necessitated the implementation of strategies that centred wellness (self/collective care) in sustaining movement building by activists pushing back against the attacks on the rights of their sexual and gender minority communities.The virtual meetings to update donors about the state of affairs in Uganda and Kenya with regards to organising and community mobilisation by structurally silenced women/communities (SSW/SSC) and how funders can further resource our communities. Changing Faces, Changing Spaces (CFCS) VIII Donor Pre-Conference brought together 78 funders from private and public foundations as well as government funding agencies such as the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Netherlands office in Maputo, Mozambique. Our flagship movement building event was held in Botswana after we had to relocate the conference to the Southern Africa region owing to the dynamic socio-political context in East Africa. 100 donors in total had expressed interest in being part of the CFCS VIII Conference. Inasmuch as there have not been direct/official engagements with Dutch Embassy in Kenya, there have been bilateral conversations with Embassy officials who were informed progressively on the socio-political situation in Kenya and how the political tensions (fueled by religion and external anti-rights actors such as CitizenGo and Family Watch International) have influenced organising by Structurally Silenced Women in Kenya. In 2023, UHAI continued this engagement through the virtual/physical Funder's and Partner's briefings as well as engagement with Embassy officials and other allied partners during the King's Day Celebrations in April 2022.
